name: trust
description:
The proposition band: the sentence that names the brand, with the lockup ON the line, and the three claims as seals under it.

The headline is display type at thesis scale — it ran at 28px once, a caption for the sentence that states what the product IS, on a page whose section headings reach 48. Its measure is in REM, not ch: `ch` is the width of the font's own zero and the display serif's zero is narrow, so 36ch measured 558px and broke the sentence to three lines.

The claims are chips, not columns: identical weight on three columns floated, '100%' repeated as the largest element carried no information, and the actual claim was set smallest. Each chip leads with its mark in the lighter sunflower — `accent-edge` at 8.42:1 on the lifted ground, with `accent-ink` inside it at 3.99:1, one hue at two strengths — then the claim in full band ink, then the figure as the annotation.

base.$description: The band itself is a `section` with `ground-primary`; this unit owns the type and the chips, not the ground. `inline-size: auto` — the parts size inside the section's own measure, and the unit adds no second container between the chips and the section width their grid reads.

lockup.$description: The logo sits ON the line: it takes the headline's size, and its two halves keep their own 0.714 ratio to each other. Baseline alignment comes from the logo unit — the display 'aven' is the taller half and centring would leave the two at different heights.

claims.$description: Composes `grid-auto center`. `--min` is the primitive's own knob for the narrowest column: 9rem, a third narrower than cards would take, because these are marks, not panels competing with the sentence above them.

claim.$description: Composes `stack surface surface--lift surface--size-chip`. `surface` is a BOX and `stack` is a LAYOUT, and they collide on one line: surface's base sets `display: block`, so the grid is re-asserted here — this unit sits after `surface` in the components layer, which is what lets it win the tie.

claim-icon.$description: The figure has to clear 3:1 against its own backing and the backing 3:1 against the chip. Against FULL sunflower nothing lighter works, so the backing moves UP the ramp instead of the figure moving down it: `accent-edge` is the lighter sunflower at 8.42:1 on the chip, and `accent-ink` sits inside it at 3.99:1.

claim-name.$description: The claim leads, the figure supports it — it was the other way round, and '100%' three times is the same word three times.

claim-figure.$description: The sans face, not the display one — the serif made it read as a second heading competing with the claim it qualifies. The same lighter sunflower as the mark, so the chip is one colour at two strengths rather than three. No opacity: this band's headroom is thin and fading ink here is what axe caught twice.

a11y.note: The headline is the section's `aria-labelledby` target, so it keeps its id alongside the part class. The claims are a real `<ul>`; each icon is `aria-hidden` because the words underneath already say what it is.
